name: FlashAttention-3 claim-support benchmark
provenance: 24 balanced, manually authored and source-checked claim/evidence pairs based on Ada's public-only FlashAttention-3 run. Evidence is paraphrased from the paper and author blog. This narrow benchmark evaluates claim-verdict behavior, not end-to-end research quality.

sources.title: FlashAttention-3: Fast and Accurate Attention with Asynchrony and Low-precision (paper)

cases.claim: FlashAttention-3 uses asynchronous Tensor Core and TMA operations to overlap computation and data movement.
evidence: The paper describes using Tensor Core and TMA asynchrony with warp specialization to overlap computation and data movement.

cases.claim: FlashAttention-3 interleaves block-wise matrix multiplication and softmax operations.
evidence: One of the paper's techniques is interleaving block-wise matrix multiplication and softmax operations.

cases.claim: On H100, FlashAttention-3 reaches up to 740 TFLOPs/s with FP16, reported as 75% utilization.
evidence: The paper reports up to 740 TFLOPs/s and 75% H100 utilization for FP16 FlashAttention-3.

cases.claim: The paper reports close to 1.2 PFLOPs/s for FlashAttention-3 with FP8.
evidence: The paper reports FP8 FlashAttention-3 performance close to 1.2 PFLOPs/s.

cases.claim: The reported FP16 speedup over FlashAttention-2 on H100 is between 1.5x and 2.0x.
evidence: The paper reports FlashAttention-3 speedups of 1.5x to 2.0x over FlashAttention-2 on H100 with FP16.

cases.claim: For FP8, the paper reports 2.6x lower numerical error than a baseline FP8 attention implementation.
evidence: The paper compares FP8 FlashAttention-3 with a baseline FP8 attention implementation and reports 2.6x lower numerical error.

cases.claim: The paper says FlashAttention-2 achieved 35% utilization on the H100 GPU.
evidence: The paper describes FlashAttention-2 as reaching 35% utilization on H100 before introducing FlashAttention-3.

cases.claim: FlashAttention-3 uses block quantization and incoherent processing to use hardware support for FP8.
evidence: The paper lists block quantization and incoherent processing among its techniques for using hardware support for low-precision FP8.

cases.claim: FlashAttention-3 makes every Transformer workload between 1.5x and 2.0x faster.
evidence: The reported 1.5x to 2.0x speedup is for attention on H100 with FP16 compared with FlashAttention-2, not every Transformer workload.

cases.claim: FlashAttention-3 reduces numerical error by 2.6x for both FP8 and FP16.
evidence: The 2.6x lower numerical error result is reported for FP8 compared with a baseline FP8 attention implementation; no FP16 error reduction is stated here.

cases.claim: FlashAttention-3 reaches 75% utilization on all Hopper GPUs.
evidence: The paper reports up to 75% utilization on the H100 GPU for FP16; it does not establish the same result on all Hopper GPUs.

cases.claim: Asynchrony alone accounts for all FlashAttention-3 performance improvements.
evidence: The paper presents multiple techniques, including asynchronous overlap, interleaving matrix multiplication and softmax, and low-precision processing.

cases.claim: FlashAttention-3 reaches exactly 740 TFLOPs/s in FP16 on every H100 configuration.
evidence: The paper reports FP16 performance up to 740 TFLOPs/s on H100; 'up to' does not mean exactly that performance for every configuration.

cases.claim: FlashAttention-3 proves FP8 is more accurate than FP16 attention.
evidence: The paper reports lower error for its FP8 implementation than a baseline FP8 attention implementation, not a comparison against FP16.

cases.claim: FlashAttention-3 delivers the same speedup on every GPU architecture.
evidence: The reported performance results are tied to Hopper H100; the excerpt does not establish equal speedups on other GPU architectures.

cases.claim: The paper establishes that FlashAttention-3 improves end-to-end LLM serving latency by 1.5x to 2.0x.
evidence: The reported 1.5x to 2.0x result compares the attention implementation against FlashAttention-2 on H100, not end-to-end LLM serving latency.

cases.claim: FlashAttention-3 reaches 740 TFLOPs/s with FP8 on H100.
evidence: The paper associates up to 740 TFLOPs/s and 75% utilization with FP16. Its FP8 result is reported separately as close to 1.2 PFLOPs/s.

cases.claim: FlashAttention-3 reaches close to 1.2 PFLOPs/s with FP16.
evidence: The paper reports close to 1.2 PFLOPs/s for FP8, while the FP16 result is up to 740 TFLOPs/s.

cases.claim: FlashAttention-3 is reported to be 10x faster than FlashAttention-2 on H100.
evidence: The reported H100 FP16 speedup over FlashAttention-2 is 1.5x to 2.0x, not 10x.

cases.claim: FlashAttention-2 reached 75% H100 utilization before FlashAttention-3.
evidence: The paper attributes 35% H100 utilization to FlashAttention-2 and up to 75% to FlashAttention-3 with FP16.

cases.claim: FlashAttention-3 reports 2.6x higher numerical error than baseline FP8 attention.
evidence: The paper reports 2.6x lower, not higher, numerical error than a baseline FP8 attention implementation.

cases.claim: The reported 740 TFLOPs/s FP16 result was measured on an A100 GPU.
evidence: The reported 740 TFLOPs/s FP16 result is on H100; the paper discusses Hopper GPUs.

cases.claim: FlashAttention-3 does not use asynchronous operations or overlap data movement with computation.
evidence: The paper explicitly describes exploiting Tensor Core and TMA asynchrony to overlap computation and data movement.

cases.claim: The paper reports FP16 FlashAttention-3 performance close to 1.2 PFLOPs/s.
evidence: The close to 1.2 PFLOPs/s result is reported for FP8; the FP16 result is up to 740 TFLOPs/s.
